blockingFindings.title: Incomplete JSON detail assertions

blockingFindings.title: Unreadable-path test may pass without exercising unreadable production behavior
blockingFindings.rationale: R2 requires indeterminate on unreadable non-excluded paths; the current test can fail to exercise that production behavior and is not reliably executable across environments.
blockingFindings.issue: The test creates `src/locked/file.js`, then removes permissions from `src/locked`. When run as a privileged user or on a filesystem/OS where chmod does not make the directory unreadable to the test process, traversal can still read it and the assertion becomes environment-dependent rather than a reliable regression test for unreadable non-excluded paths.
blockingFindings.requiredChange: Make the unreadable-path test deterministic for the supported test environment, for example by using a controlled filesystem error seam/mock if one exists, or by isolating this assertion behind a reliable platform/permission precondition.
blockingFindings.whyBlocking: R2 requires indeterminate on unreadable non-excluded paths; the current test can fail to exercise that production behavior and is not reliably executable across environments.

blockingFindings.title: R4 generated maxFiles coverage is incomplete
blockingFindings.rationale: An explicit acceptance requirement has no corresponding spec-local test coverage for several required excluded paths under the stated over-budget fresh/stale condition.
blockingFindings.issue: R4 requires unit tests where `.senti`, `node_modules`, `vendor`, `.git`, and generated specs evidence each contain more than `maxFiles` files while source and docs still return fresh or stale. The tests only put more-than-budget files in these paths collectively in the R1 stale case, and only `.senti/output` in the R4 fresh case. There is no fresh/stale assertion proving `node_modules`, `vendor`, `.git`, `specs/*/review-history`, `specs/*/review-evidence`, and `specs/*/tests/.raw` remain ignored under the over-budget condition in the R4 scenario.

blockingFindings.whyBlocking: An explicit acceptance requirement has no corresponding spec-local test coverage for several required excluded paths under the stated over-budget fresh/stale condition.

An implementation could incorrectly use the default 10,000-file budget for excluded directories and still pass these tests.

requirements.desc: Define the named freshness source policy `freshness-source`. It skips a directory before recursion when its basename is .git, .senti, node_modules, or vendor; it also skips a path matching specs/*/review-history, specs/*/review-evidence, or specs/*/tests/.raw. Every other source-root directory remains traversed and counted.

Use that policy only for sourceRoot traversal. Traverse docs/ without source exclusions; return indeterminate if either scan reaches maxDepth 32, maxDirectoryEntries 10,000, maxFiles 10,000, or an unreadable non-excluded path.

Add sourceScan and docsScan JSON details, each containing target, policy name, complete, and limits with kind, relativePath, and maximum. Keep result names and retain toText labels: fresh, stale with docs-build guidance, never-built with docs-build guidance, and indeterminate with limits.

Add unit tests in which .senti, node_modules, vendor, .git, and generated specs evidence contain more than maxFiles files but source and docs still return fresh or stale; separately prove that a limit in non-excluded source or docs returns indeterminate.
